doc.title: Eddie Alley interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Francisco, California, August 8, 2002

title: His brother's career, Jo Jones in New York and Sweet's Ballroom
summary: The brother played with Basie, Hampton and Vaughan, while Alley stayed local; Jo Jones showed him New York and he played Sweet's Ballroom.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: There was three of us. My sister died some years ago. There was three of us, my brother — my brother is a big shot — not me, I’m the little guy. He is the one that played with Count Basie and Lionel Hampton and Sarah Vaughan and all the big people. I just played locally. I’m the little guy.
Yeah but you had your role.

Oh I did little things. I did my little number. I says, the names I’ve met, these people I came in contact with. But I didn’t travel like he did you know or things like that. And the people I did meet really liked me a lot like Ben Webster and Dizzy. They really took a liking to me for some reason and we got along great. In fact when I first went to New York Jo Jones, Papa Jo Jones the drummer with Basie, he took me all over New York. So I always got along great with these great musicians.
Um hum, I played in Sweet’s Ballroom in Oakland, I played over there.
